questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Explore new cultures

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: The city and school that I was going to study at and in. I wanted a place that could challenge me and expand my knowledge and understanding, and a destination rich on new experiences. I wanted to improve my english skills for my master degree as well, so it was important that it was an english speaking country.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: It was very hard. I felt alone in the proces and I was in distress with the visa, payment for the school and the sign up for classes where we were put last in line for registration which I found weird when we would only be able to participate in classes for one semester. I found the resources at my home university lackfull in regarding to the specific deal KU has with Barnard.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: I studied at Barnard College in New York City where they had a welcoming program for international students called VISP and a resource at the school called Acces Barnard that introduced us to and helped us navigate a new university. Yet, not all times was this resource helpfull.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: Different dormrooms were offered, but it was mandatory to live on campus as an exchange student.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: We had a kitchen and it was mandatory with a meal plan. Here we could choose from different sizes of meal plans.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer:
That the different dorm rooms vary a lot. Some are big with many facilities while others are small. We where lucky to live in Cathedral Gardens which was more apartment than corridor style. 

Some of the apartments are not very clean and that was a culture shock coming from Denmark where the general level of cleanness is higher.

The dormrooms are very expensive and you will most likely share a room with another person.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: There is a 14 days shopping period, were you try out classes, but all the students studying at the school has already signed up for classes, so you are put last in line and need to fight and try to convince the professors to give you a spot. This was very stressfull in a time where everything is new, so I think that we should be able register beforehand just as the other students. It is a little nervewrecking travelling to the other side of the world for your education not even knowing if you will be able to take classes that will be approved or even are relevant to your field of study.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: Counselors and deans were helpful, but the proces is just so bad that often they couldn't do anything about the fact that classes were full.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got classes that was relevant for me, but many of the classes I had looked at back home didn't have available spots when I got there which was a shame. Some of my classes weren't the ones I wanted and that was a big shame because I think I would have learned a lot from those.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Before going, ty to see if you can find the emails for the professors of the classes you want and then email them to tell them about your situation and see if you can get a spot on the waitlist or in the class. Often they are helpfull and this seemed like a normal procedure.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level of the different courses varies a lot and I was taking both introductionary courses and graduate courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: Different from back home, feels more like going to gymnasium where you have a big workload throughout the semester and has to do a lot of tests assignments and quizzes that you are graded for as well.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Introduction to architectural history
Urban ecosystems
Design futures: New York City
Urban ecology and design

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Depends on what you study. I really enjoyed the professor of design futures; Ivan Munuera! and the professor in Urban ecosystems Elizabeth Cook. Urban ecology and design was also interesting with nice field trips

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: We needed to pay some extra money for the welcoming week and programme made for us during this time. Also the VISA for USA is very expensive and an extra travel insurance was needed.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: It is a very expensive city to live in in general so everything adds up when you go out with taxes and tips.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of clubs and a gym.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I didn't try out as many, but it was fun to go and watch the schools basketball games.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Explore New York City, go upstate on a roadtrip

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Yes, New York is such a nice (but also a little crazy) place

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Hard to do group work in class.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: Diversity and many experiences around every corner.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: It will sort out with classes and enjoy the city as much as possible.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Try to email professors beforehand.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Living in a new environment and getting to know new people and a new way of studying.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: All the stuff before the stay, planning, registration, etc.

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
